rows.speaker: ابن زيد والفراء
rows.claim: They supply an ellipsis, understanding the phrase as saying no one in heaven can escape God's power if disobedient.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن زيد، والفراء: التقدير: ولا من في السماء

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ calls this deletion a subtle Arabic construction and cites Ḥassān's verse for omitting a relative pronoun while retaining its clause.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: وهذا من غوامض العربية، وأنشد قول حسان

rows.speaker: البصريون
rows.claim: The Basrans allow deletion of the relative pronoun with its clause retained only in poetry.
rows.anchor: لأن فيه حذف الموصول وإبقاء صلته. وأبعد من هذا القول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He calls especially far-fetched an alternative: humans and jinn on earth, and angels in heaven, cannot escape God.
rows.anchor: وأبعد من هذا القول قول من زعم أن التقدير

rows.speaker: الجمهور وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce يئسوا with hamza; Abū Jaʿfar reads it without hamza, replacing it with yāʾ.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: يئسوا، بالهمز والذماري، وأبو جعفر: بغير همز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning means they will despair on Judgment Day; reported alternatives specify despair of God's mercy or religion and thus His guidance.
rows.anchor: وهو وعيد، أي ييأسون يوم القيامة. وقيل: من رحمتي. وقيل: من ديني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation describes unbelievers' disposition: unlike believers, who remain hopeful and fearful, they do not consider this prospect; their state resembles despair of mercy.
rows.anchor: لأن المؤمن يكون دائما راجيا خائفا، والكافر لا يخطر بباله ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes وإن تكذبوا through عذاب أليم as God's words quoting Abraham; another view treats these verses as a divine parenthesis between Abraham's speech and his people's reply.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن قول: وإن تكذبوا، من كلام الله، حكاية عن إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the parenthesis reading, it consoles Muhammad by recalling Abraham's trial with idolatrous people who rejected and tried to kill him; the following verses establish monotheism, God's signs, power, and resurrection.
rows.anchor: وفائدة هذا الاعتراض أنه تسلية للرسول صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Abraham's proof against idolatry, his people substituted force for an answer; some urged killing him, others burning him, hoping the fire would make him recant or kill him.
rows.anchor: رجعوا إلى الغلبة، فجعلوا القائم مقام جوابه فيما أمرهم به قولهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An omitted phrase means they threw Abraham into the fire, but God saved him; his burning story was discussed earlier in Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام حذف، أي حرقوه في النار، فأنجاه الله من النار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural signs suits several signs in Abraham's rescue: the fire became cool and safe, burned only his bonds, and, in a reported account, the site became a garden; rescue from the ship was one sign.
rows.anchor: وجمع هنا فقال: الآيات، لأن الإنجاء من النار، وجعلها بردا وسلاما

rows.speaker: كعب
rows.claim: Kaʿb says the fire burned only the rope with which Abraham had been bound.
rows.anchor: قال كعب: لم يحترق بالنار إلا الحبل الذي أوثقوه به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The kill-or-burn alternatives may reflect two groups making separate proposals; Sūrat al-Anbiyāʾ names only burning, the option they carried out.
rows.anchor: فقد يكون ذلك من قائلين: ناس أشاروا بالقتل، وناس أشاروا بالإحراق

rows.speaker: الجمهور والحسن وسالم الأفطس
rows.claim: The majority and al-Ḥasan read جواب in the accusative; Sālim al-Afṭas reads it nominative as the predicate of كان.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: جواب، بالنصب والحسن، وسالم الأفطس: بالرفع

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو حيوة وابن أبي عبلة وأبو عمرو والأعمش
rows.claim: These readers raise مودة and put بينكم in the accusative; the raising can make it the predicate of إن, with ما relative, a verbal noun, or a prepared particle after an omitted subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن، وأبو حيوة، وابن أبي عبلة، وأبو عمرو في رواية الأصمعي

rows.speaker: عاصم
rows.claim: ʿĀṣim is reported to raise مودة without nunation and read بينكم with an open nūn, treating it as built through annexation to an indeclinable form.
rows.anchor: وروي عن عاصم: مودة، بالرفع من غير تنوين وبينكم بالفتح

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والكسائي وابن كثير
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr, al-Kisāʾī, and Ibn Kathīr have the same raised reading but pronounce the nūn of بينكم with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو، والكسائي، وابن كثير: كذلك، إلا أنه خفض نون بينكم

rows.speaker: ابن عامر وعاصم وحمزة
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir and ʿĀṣim read مودة with accusative and nunation and بينكم accusative; Ḥamza instead annexes مودة to بينكم and lowers it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر، وعاصم: بنصب مودة منونا ونصب بينكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: اتخذ may govern two objects, with مودة as the second: idols were adopted because of mutual affection or as its cause; alternatively, it governs one object and مودة gives the purpose of gathering to worship them.
rows.anchor: أي اتخذتم الأوثان بسبب المودة بينكم، على حذف المضاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd is credited with a noncanonical reading unlike the written codex, but Abū Ḥayyān omits it because sound, widespread transmission from him also preserves the codex reading.
rows.anchor: وذكروا عن ابن مسعود قراءة شاذة تخالف سواد المصحف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The idol worshippers and their idols will curse one another at Resurrection, as in the verse about them becoming enemies to their worshippers.
rows.anchor: ثم يوم القيامة يقع بينكم التلاعن، أي فيلاعن العبدة والمعبودات الأصنام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: في الحياة and بينكم can both modify مودة as different kinds of adverbial, or attach to omitted words and describe its state.
rows.anchor: وبينكم، وفي الحياة: يجوز تعليقهما بلفظ مودة وعمل في ظرفين

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ allows في الحياة to attach to اتخذتم when ما is redundant and مودة is accusative, but not with the relative or verbal-noun analyses that raise مودة.
rows.anchor: وأجاز أبو البقاء أن يتعلق في الحياة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya and others attach في الحياة to مودة and make بينكم its adjective; Abū Ḥayyān rejects this because a verbal noun cannot govern before taking its complements.
rows.anchor: وأجاز قوم منهم ابن عطية أن يتعلق في الحياة بمودة

rows.speaker: أبو البقاء
rows.claim: Abū al-Baqāʾ also proposes attaching في الحياة to بينكم or making it a state of بينكم; Abū Ḥayyān says neither parsing is intelligible.
rows.anchor: وأجاز أيضا أن يجعله حالا من بينكم، قال: لتعرفه بالإضافة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot alone among Abraham's people believed in him after seeing the fire fail to burn him; Lot was either Sarah's brother's son or her cousin.
rows.anchor: لم يؤمن بإبراهيم أحد من قومه إلا لوط عليه السلام، حين رأى النار لم تحرقه

rows.speaker: قتادة والنخعي
rows.claim: The pronoun in وقال returns to Abraham, matching ووهبنا له; Qatāda and al-Nakhaʿī are cited for this, while another group returns it to Lot.
rows.anchor: والضمير في وقال عائد على إبراهيم، وهو الظاهر، ليتناسق مع قوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A group says Abraham and Lot migrated from Kutha in Babylonian Iraq to Palestine; Abraham was seventy-five and the first to migrate for God. Ibn Jurayj instead places an intermediate move to Harran and says Sarah accompanied him.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: يعود على لوط، وهاجر، وإبراهيم، عليهم السلام، من قريتهما كوثى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Migrant literally means one who leaves something; in religious usage it is one who leaves home seeking God's pleasure, and the title Muhājirūn was used for the companions before Mecca's conquest.
rows.anchor: والمهاجر: الفارغ عن الشيء، وهو في عرف الشريعة: من ترك وطنه رغبة في رضا الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations of إلى ربي are migrating to somewhere one can worship without obstruction, or leaving opponents among his people to draw near to God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إلى حيث لا أمنع عبادة ربي. وقيل: مهاجرا من خالفني من قومي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham settled in Palestine and left Lot in Sodom, the overturned city about a day and night's journey away; العزيز cannot be overcome and الحكيم puts things in their proper places.
rows.anchor: ونزل إبراهيم قرية من أرض فلسطين، وترك لوطا في سدوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in ذريته refers to Abraham; his descendants included Isaac, Jacob, Israelite prophets, Ishmael, and Muhammad, while الكتاب collectively denotes the Torah, Psalms, Gospel, and Qur'an.
rows.anchor: والضمير في ذريته عائد على إبراهيم. النبوة: إسحاق، ويعقوب

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid identifies Abraham's worldly reward as rescue from the fire and the tyrant king, righteous work, and praise such that every community takes him as a protector.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: نجاته من النار، ومن الملك الجبار، والعمل الصالح

rows.speaker: ابن جريج والحسن
rows.claim: Ibn Jurayj says the reward was the child who gladdened Abraham's eye; al-Ḥasan is named in connection with this view.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جريج: والولد الذي قرت به عينه، قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says Abraham was shown his place in Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: إنه رأى مكانه من الجنة

rows.speaker: ابن أبي بردة
rows.claim: Ibn Abī Burda says the reward was success in deeds of the afterlife.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن أبي بردة: ما وفق له من عمل الآخرة

rows.speaker: الماوردي
rows.claim: Al-Māwardī says Abraham's reward was the continued hospitality offered at his grave, unique among the prophets.
rows.anchor: وقال الماوردي: بقاء ضيافته عند قبره، وليس ذلك لنبي غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other reported meanings of Abraham's reward are prophethood and wisdom, or blessings and prayers upon him until the end of time.
rows.anchor: وقيل: النبوة والحكمة. وقيل: الصلاة عليه إلى آخر الدهر

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most readers pronounce both أإنكم clauses as questions; another reading makes the first declarative and the second interrogative. Abū ʿUbayd reports their different letter counts in the codex.
rows.anchor: والجمهور: على الاستفهام في أئنكم معا. وقرىء: أنكم على الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot's account does not repeat a call to worship God because he belonged to Abraham's people and Abraham had already made monotheism famous; Abraham and Shuʿayb had to call later peoples to worship God.
rows.anchor: ولم يأت في قصة لوط أنه دعا قومه إلى عبادة الله

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī reads ما سبقكم بها as a confirming independent clause: no people before Lot's had committed the act because its extreme ugliness repelled human nature.
rows.anchor: قال الزمخشري: ما سبقكم بها جملة مستأنفة مقررة لفاحشة تلك الفعلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyān prefers a circumstantial reading: they commit the act as its inventors, without precedent; both questions are rebuking, and the wording specifies anal intercourse with men.
rows.anchor: ويظهر أن ما سبقكم بها جملة حالية، كأنه قال: أتأتون الفاحشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وتقطعون السبيل is explained as ending procreation through anal sex, deterring travelers, robbery and murder, or ruining trade through their notoriety.
rows.anchor: وتقطعون السبيل: الولد، بتعطيل الفرج ووطء أدبار الرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: نادي means a meeting place and is generic because the towns had many; strictly it is called a club only while its people are assembled, and afterward only figuratively.
rows.anchor: وتأتون في ناديكم: أي في مجلسكم الذي تجتمعون فيه، وهو اسم جنس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: المنكر is whatever reason, religious law, or good character condemns; reported acts include pelting people with pebbles and mocking an unfamiliar stranger, with a report from Umm Hāni tracing to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: والمنكر: ما تنكره العقول والشرائع والمروءات، حذف الناس بالحصباء

rows.speaker: منصور ومجاهد والقاسم بن محمد وقتادة بن زيد
rows.claim: They explain the public wrongdoing as men having intercourse in their gathering where others could watch.
rows.anchor: قاله منصور ومجاهد والقاسم بن محمد وقتادة بن زيد أو تضارطهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās lists farting and clapping in the assembly as further meanings of the wrongdoing.
rows.anchor: أو تضارطهم أو تصافعهم فيها، قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid also lists pigeon play, henna on fingertips, whistling, pebble play, and abandoning modesty in all their conduct.
rows.anchor: أو لعب الحمام أو تطريف الأصابع بالحناء، والصفير، والحذف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās also names pebble-shooting, finger-popping, gum chewing, using a toothstick in public, unfastening clothes, obscene joking, and other indecencies alongside idolatry.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن عباس أيضا مع شركهم بالله. كانت فيهم ذنوب غير الفاحشة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their other wrongs included mutual oppression, backgammon and chess, conspicuous dyed clothing, men dressing as women, and levies on every traveler; they were first to practice male and female same-sex intercourse.
rows.anchor: ولعب بالنرد والشطرنج، ولبس المصبغات، ولباس النساء للرجال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Lot exposed these vices, his people persisted in denial and demanded punishment while convinced his warning was false.
rows.anchor: أصروا على اللجاج في التكذيب، فكان جوابهم له: أن قالوا ائتنا بعذاب الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lot then sought help, so angels were sent to punish his people with stoning hail and to corrupt them by making them commit sins, especially their invented sexual vice.
rows.anchor: ثم استنصر لوط عليه السلام، فبعث ملائكة لعذابهم، ورجمهم بالحاصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The glad tidings to Abraham were Isaac, grandson Jacob, and support for Lot through the destruction of Lot's people; the town was Sodom.
rows.anchor: بالبشرى: هي بشارته بولده إسحاق، وبنافلته يعقوب، وبنصر لوط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: كانوا ظالمين means they had already committed and persisted in wrongdoing, including unbelief and varied sins; Sodom also figures in a proverb about an unjust judge.
rows.anchor: والقرية: سدوم، وفيها قيل: أجور من قاضي سدوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Abraham worried because Lot was in the doomed town; when he said a guiltless Lot was there, the angels replied that they knew its inhabitants better than he did and would save Lot and family except his wife.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكروا لإبراهيم: إنا مهلكوا أهل هذه القرية، أشفق على لوط

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read لننجينه from أنجى, while the other six of the seven use نجّى; the majority lengthen the nūn and another group lightens it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة، والكسائي: لننجينه، مضارع أنجى وباقي السبعة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the extra أن after لما emphasizes that events followed immediately, as Lot sensed the visitors and was suddenly distressed; this fits Sībawayh's view of لما as a particle, against al-Fārisī.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري أن صلة أكدت وجود الفعلين مترتبا أحدهما على الآخر

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sībawayh treats لما as a particle rather than an adverbial noun, the grammatical position tied to the discussion of added أن.
rows.anchor: وهذا الذي ذكره في الترتيب هو مذهب سيبويه، إذ مذهبه

rows.speaker: العربيان ونافع وحفص
rows.claim: The two Arab readers, Nāfiʿ, and Ḥafṣ read منجوك with doubled jīm; the remaining seven readers lighten it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العربيان، ونافع، وحفص: منجوك، مشددا وباقي السبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Under Sībawayh's parsing the kāf is genitive and أهلك accusative after an omitted verb; al-Akhfash and Hishām instead take the kāf as accusative and coordinate أهلك with it.
rows.anchor: والكاف في مذهب سيبويه في موضع جر. وأهلك: منصوب على إضمار فعل

rows.speaker: نافع وابن عامر والكسائي
rows.claim: They read سيء with the sīn rounded; ʿĪsā and Ṭalḥa read سوء in the Hudhayl dialect, also changing vowels in قيل and بيع.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: سيء، بكسر السين وضمها نافع وابن عامر والكسائي

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة والأعمش وابن محيصن
rows.claim: The passage reports light and doubled منزلون, Ibn Muḥayṣin's رجزا with rounded rāʾ, and Abū Ḥayyah and al-Aʿmash's kasra in يفسقون.
rows.anchor: وقرىء: منزلون، مخففا ومشددا وابن محيصن: رجزا، بضم الراء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: If منها refers to the town, Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the sign as its ruined houses; Abū Sulaymān describes foundations still above and roofs below.
rows.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في منها عائد على القرية، فقال ابن عباس: منازلهم الخربة

rows.speaker: الفراء
rows.claim: Al-Farrāʾ takes the meaning as leaving the town as a sign, treating من as extra in a positive clause; Abū Ḥayyān says this only works with that unusual grammatical allowance.
rows.anchor: وقال الفراء: المعنى تركناها آية، يقول: إن في السماء لآية

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: If منها refers to the punishment inflicted on them, Qatāda says the sign was stones that reached the earliest Muslims.
rows.anchor: فقيل: الآية: الحجارة التي أدركتها أوائل هذه الأمة، قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the sign was black water left on the earth.
rows.anchor: قاله قتادة وقيل: الماء الأسود على وجه الأرض، قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation says the sign was the very outcome of what had been done to them.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أنجز ما صنع بهم. ولقوم: متعلق بتركنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their denial brings the earthquake, and they are left dead in their homes.
rows.anchor: فأخذتهم الرجفة فأصبحوا في دارهم جاثمين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The ruined dwellings show the punishment because Meccans passed by them on their journeys.
rows.anchor: وكان أهل مكة يمرون عليها في أسفارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Satan adorned their ugly deeds by whispering and diverted them from faith in God and His messengers.
rows.anchor: وزين لهم الشيطان: أي بوسوسته وإغوائه، أعمالهم القبيحة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عاد وثمود may be accusative after an implied أهلكنا, coordinated with the pronoun in فأخذتهم, or—more remotely—with الذين earlier; another reading puts them genitive as recipients of a mission.
rows.anchor: وانتصب وعادا وثمود بإضمار أهلكنا، لدلالة فأخذتهم الرجفة عليه

rows.speaker: حمزة وشيبة والحسن وحفص
rows.claim: They leave ثمود without nunation; the other seven nunate it, while Ibn Waththāb reads both names genitive and nunated.
rows.anchor: وقرأ: ثمود، بغير تنوين حمزة، وشيبة، والحسن، وحفص

rows.speaker: الأعمش
rows.claim: Al-Aʿmash reads مساكنهم in the nominative without من, making it the subject of تبين.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الأعمش: مساكنهم، بالرفع من غير من

rows.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد والضحاك
rows.claim: They understand مستبصرين as people with insight into and admiration for their unbelief; another view says they knew the message was true but rejected it defiantly.
rows.anchor: قاله، ابن عباس، ومجاهد، والضحاك. وقيل: عقلاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qārūn may coordinate with prior names or follow an implied اذكر; their arrogance was refusal of the Creator and His worship, irrational for weak earthly beings, and they were not the first peoples to disbelieve.
rows.anchor: وقارون: معطوف على ما قبله، أو منصوب بإضمار اذكر. فاستكبروا

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Punishments are mapped to their peoples: hail to Lot, a blast to Midian and Thamūd, swallowing to Qārūn, and drowning to Noah's and Pharaoh's peoples; Ibn ʿAṭiyya thinks ʿĀd may also have faced hail-bearing wind.
rows.anchor: والحاصب لقوم لوط، وهي ريح عاصف فيها حصا، وقيل: ملك كان يرميهم

rows.speaker: الفرزدق
rows.claim: Al-Farazdaq's line uses بحاصب for a wind hurling debris like scattered cotton, illustrating the word's sense.
rows.anchor:
ومنه قول الفرزدق:
مستقبلين شمال الشام تضربهم ... بحاصب كنديف القطن منثور

rows.speaker: الأخطل
rows.claim: Al-Akhṭal's line uses بحاصب for fruit cast from trees, another poetic illustration of the word.
rows.anchor:
ومنه قول الأخطل:
ترمي العضاة بحاصب من بلحها ... حتى تبيت على العضاه حفالا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: عنكبوت has the stated Arabic pattern, may be masculine or feminine, has plural عناكب and diminutive عنيكيب; a quoted poet supplies evidence for masculine agreement.
rows.anchor: العنكبوت: حيوان معروف، ووزنه فعللوت، ويؤنث ويذكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The apparent comparison is a person relying on a patron besides God and a spider relying on its web: neither gives dependable shelter, and idols provide no benefit.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر، هو تشبيه المتخذ من دون الله وليا، بالعنكبوت المتخذة بيتا

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī takes the comparison as idols people rely on resembling the weak web; the phrase about the weakest house signals this focus.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: الغرض تشبيه ما اتخذوه متكلا ومعتمدا في دينهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The spider's house is useless and extremely flimsy just as idols cannot help; لو كانوا يعلمون means knowing their religion was this weak would make them abandon idols, not that anyone needs to be told webs are fragile.
rows.anchor: وقوله: لو كانوا يعلمون، ليس مرتبطا بقوله: وإن أوهن البيوت لبيت العنكبوت

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī extends the comparison: if the spider web is the weakest house, idol worship is the weakest religion, contrasted with a solid human-built house.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: إذا صح تشبيه ما اعتمدوه في دينهم ببيت العنكبوت

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وسلام
rows.claim: Abū ʿAmr and Sallām assimilate consonants in يعلم ما; most readers keep them distinct.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو، وسلام: يعلم ما، بالإدغام والجمهور: بالفك

rows.speaker: الجمهور وأبو عمرو وعاصم
rows.claim: Most read تدعون in the second person; Abū ʿAmr and ʿĀṣim, in one transmission, read it in the third person.
rows.anchor: والجمهور: تدعون، بتاء الخطاب وأبو عمرو، وعاصم: بخلاف، بياء الغيبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما may be the object of يدعون, meaning God knows the false objects they invoke; it may instead negate that they invoke anything of worth, or be a reproachful question interrupting the sentence.
rows.anchor: وجوزوا في ما أن يكون مفعولا بيدعون، أي يعلم الذين يدعون

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abū ʿAlī treats ما as an interrogative object of يدعون and makes يعلم govern the whole clause: God knows whether they call idols or something else.
rows.anchor: وجوز أبو علي أن يكون ما استفهاما منصوبا بيدعون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question reading reiterates the parable; the negative reading adds that what they invoke is not even worthy of being called a thing.
rows.anchor: والجملة تأكيد للمثل، وإذا كانت ما نافية، كان في الجملة زيادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling God العزيز الحكيم exposes the folly of worshipping inert things without knowledge or power instead of the sovereign, wise God.
rows.anchor: فيه تجهيل لهم، حيث عبدوا ما ليس بشيء، لأنه جماد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Only the learned grasp the truth and benefit of these parables; Quraysh's mockery of comparisons to flies and spiders missed how figures make hidden meanings perceptible.
rows.anchor: وكان جهلة قريش يقولون: إن رب محمد يضرب المثل بالذباب والعنكبوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: وتلك الأمثال points to this comparison and the earlier parables in other sūras.
rows.anchor: والإشارة بقوله: وتلك الأمثال إلى هذا المثل، وما تقدم من الأمثال

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jābir reports that when the Prophet recited this verse he defined the learned person as one who understands God, obeys Him, and avoids His displeasure.
rows.anchor: وعن جابر، أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، تلا هذه الآية فقال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Creating the heavens and earth in truth means for an enduring purpose rather than play; this highlights the idols' insignificance and creation as a sign of God's power and wisdom.
rows.anchor: ومعنى بالحق: بالواجب الثابت، لا بالعبث واللعب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is the familiar ritual prayer, which restrains from indecency when performed with its obligations, sunnahs, humility, reflection, and awareness of standing before God.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: من شأنها أنها إذا أديت على ما يجب من فروضها وسننها

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والكلبي وابن جريج وحماد بن أبي سليمان
rows.claim: They say prayer restrains from evil while the worshipper is engaged in it.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس، والكلبي، وابن جريج، وحماد بن أبي سليمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A worshipper seen committing sins does not pray in the manner described, so the verse does not promise that every prayer always restrains.
rows.anchor: وأما من تراه من المصلين يتعاطى المعاصي

rows.speaker: ابن بحر
rows.claim: Ibn Baḥr interprets الصلاة as supplication, meaning to direct supplication toward God's command.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن بحر: الصلاة: الدعاء، أي أقم الدعاء إلى أمر الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A person's sinning does not disprove the verse: it says prayer has the characteristic of restraining, not that every prayer always does so; prayer must be of the described kind.
rows.anchor: ولا يدل اللفظ على أن كل صلاة تنهى، بل المعنى، أنه يوجد ذلك فيها

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: A report says an Anṣārī youth who prayed with the Prophet nevertheless committed indecencies and theft; the Prophet said his prayer would restrain him, and the youth soon repented.
rows.anchor: وفي الحديث أن فتى من الأنصار كان يصلي مع النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله وسلمان وأبو الدرداء وابن عباس وأبو قرة
rows.claim: They interpret ولذكر الله أكبر as God's remembrance of people being greater than their remembrance of Him.
rows.anchor: فقال عبد الله، وسلمان، وأبو الدرداء، وابن عباس، وأبو قرة

rows.speaker: قتادة وابن زيد
rows.claim: Qatāda and Ibn Zayd understand God's remembrance as greater than everything.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة، وابن زيد: أكبر من كل شيء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other views say remembrance in prayer earns greater reward than outside prayer, exceeds other pillars of prayer, or that God's remembrance is stronger than prayer's restraint and greater than all worship.
rows.anchor: وقيل: ولذكر الله في الصلاة أكبر منه خارج الصلاة

rows.speaker: ابن عطية
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya takes remembrance as greater without qualification: mindful remembrance restrains inside or outside prayer, whereas bodily movements have no such effect and mere speech ranks lower.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: وعندي أن المعنى: ولذكر الله أكبر على الإطلاق

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says prayer is greater than other acts of obedience, is itself called God's remembrance, and reminds people that God sees their deeds and will reward or punish them.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: يريد والصلاة أكبر من غيرها من الطاعات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ahl al-Kitāb means Jews and Christians; debate with them gently by inviting them to God and drawing attention to His signs.
rows.anchor: وأهل الكتاب: اليهود والنصارى. إلا بالتي هي أحسن: من الملاطفة في الدعاء إلى الله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: One explanation restricts the exception to those refusing jizya, waging war, or openly attributing a child, partner, or deficiency to God; on this account the truce rule was abrogated.
rows.anchor: ممن لم يؤد جزية ونصب الحرب، وصرح بأن لله ولدا أو شريكا

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd takes the exception as those persisting in unbelief, including Qurayẓa and Naḍīr; this reading leaves the verse operative.
rows.anchor: قاله ابن زيد، والآية على هذا محكمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view limits the exception to those who harmed the Prophet; Qatāda says it was abrogated by the command to fight the People of the Book.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إلا الذين آذوا رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم. وقال قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reads ألا as an attention particle rather than إلا as an exception, yielding the command to debate them in the best manner.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: إلا، حرف استثناء وابن عباس: ألا، حرف تنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying Muslims believe what was sent to both communities is itself gracious debate; what was sent to Muslims is the Qur'an and to them the Torah, Psalms, and Gospel.
rows.anchor: وقولوا آمنا: هذا من المجادلة بالأحسن. بالذي أنزل إلينا، وهو القرآن

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: In a sound al-Bukhārī report, Jews read the Torah in Hebrew and interpreted it in Arabic for Muslims; the Prophet said neither to affirm nor deny them, but to affirm what God revealed.
rows.anchor: وفي صحيح البخاري، عن أبي هريرة: كان أهل الكتاب يقرأون التوراة بالعبرانية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Just as earlier scriptures were sent down, the Qur'an was sent to Muhammad; scripture recipients may be ʿAbd Allāh ibn Salām and his companions, while من هؤلاء refers to the Meccans.
rows.anchor: فالذين آتيناهم الكتاب هم: عبد الله بن سلام ومن آمن معه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, earlier People of the Book believed the Qur'an because their scriptures foretold its messenger, and those among them in Muhammad's time also believed; only unbelievers deny the signs.
rows.anchor: وقيل: فالذين آتيناهم الكتاب: أي الذين تقدموا عهد الرسول

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujāhid says the People of the Book read in their scriptures that Muhammad could neither read nor write; من before كتاب is extra under negation.
rows.anchor: قال مجاهد: كان أهل الكتاب يقرأون في كتبهم أن محمدا عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denial of reading and writing, including the hand used to write, strengthens the proof: an unlettered man unconnected to scholars brought eloquent revelation, past history, and hidden information beyond human ability.
rows.anchor: أخذ يحقق، كونه نازلا من عند الله، بأنه ظهر عن رجل أمي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most Muslims maintain that the Prophet never wrote or read from a book.
rows.anchor: وأكثر المسلمين على أن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم لم يكتب قط

rows.speaker: الشعبي
rows.claim: Al-Shaʿbī reportedly said the Prophet did not die until he had written; al-Naqqāsh supports the report.
rows.anchor: وروي عن الشعبي أنه قال: ما مات رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، حتى كتب

rows.speaker: أبو كبشة السلولي
rows.claim: Abū Kabsha al-Sulūlī reports that the Prophet read a document belonging to ʿUyayna ibn Ḥiṣn and explained its meaning.
rows.anchor: حديث أبي كبشة السلولي: أنه صلى الله عليه وسلم، قرأ صحيفة لعيينة ابن حصن

rows.speaker: أبو ذر الهروي والباجي
rows.claim: Some, including Abū Dharr al-Harawī and al-Bājī, understand a report in Ṣaḥīḥ Muslim to mean the Prophet wrote directly; many local scholars fiercely condemned al-Bājī for it.
rows.anchor: وقد ذهب إلى ذلك جماعة، منهم أبو ذر عبد الله بن أحمد الهروي

rows.speaker: أكثر العلماء
rows.claim: Most scholars interpret the report that he wrote as meaning he ordered the writing, as in ordinary Arabic usage where a ruler's writing to someone means he ordered a letter.
rows.anchor: وتأول أكثر العلماء ما ورد من أنه كتب على أن معناه: أمر بالكتابة

rows.speaker: قتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Qatāda identifies the falsifiers who would have doubted Muhammad's revelation as the People of the Book; Mujāhid identifies them as Quraysh unbelievers.
rows.anchor: والمبطلون: أهل الكتاب، قاله قتادة أو كفار قريش، قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Had Muhammad read or written earlier books, opponents could allege he learned the Qur'an from them; since he did neither, their doubts have no basis.
rows.anchor: لو كان يقرأ كتبا قبل نزول القرآن عليه، أو يكتب، لحصلت الريبة للمبطلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an consists of clear, miraculous signs firmly preserved in the breasts of the learned and publicly recited by the wider community, unlike ordinary books kept on pages.
rows.anchor: آيات بينات: واضحات الإعجاز، في صدور الذين أوتوا العلم

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: ʿAbd Allāh's reading has هي rather than هو, making the signs feminine plural.
rows.anchor: وكونه القرآن، يؤيده قراءة عبد الله

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatāda offers an alternative referent for هو: the Prophet himself and his circumstances are clear signs.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل هو، أي النبي وأموره، آيات بينات، قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation makes the sign the Prophet's inability to read and write; the paired terms for denial can refer respectively to denial of God's oneness and prophethood.
rows.anchor: وقيل: بل هو، أي كونه لا يقرأ ولا يكتب. ويقال: جحدته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling deniers wrongdoers rather than unbelievers emphasizes rejection of prophethood after proof of the Qur'an's revelation to an unlettered messenger.
rows.anchor: وهذه بالظالمين، لأنه جحد بعد إقامة الدليل على كونه الرسول

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The Arab readers, Nāfiʿ, and Ḥafṣ read آيات in the plural; the other seven read it singular.
rows.anchor: وقرأ العربيان، ونافع، وحفص: آيات، على الجمع، وباقي السبعة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some Quraysh and Jews prompted the demand for a sign like Moses' staff; God alone chooses which signs to send, while Muhammad is a clear warner.
rows.anchor: أي قريش، وبعض اليهود كانوا يعلمون قريشا مثل هذا الاقتراح

rows.speaker: يحيى بن جعدة
rows.claim: Yaḥyā ibn Jaʿda says Muslims brought the Prophet written excerpts of Jewish sayings; he rejected them as a people's error in preferring another prophet's teaching, and أولم يكفهم was revealed.
rows.anchor: وذكر يحيى بن جعدة أن ناسا من المسلمين أتوا رسول الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse most likely answers those demanding signs: the continuously recited Qur'an is a lasting sign in every place and age, a great mercy and reminder, unlike temporary signs.
rows.anchor: والذي يظهر أنه رد على الذين قالوا: لولا أنزل عليه آيات من ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse addresses Jews: Qur'an recitation confirms what their scriptures say about Muhammad and his religion.
rows.anchor: وقيل: أولم يكفهم: يعني اليهود، أنا أنزلنا عليك الكتاب يتلى عليهم

rows.speaker: كعب بن الأشرف وأصحابه
rows.claim: Kaʿb ibn al-Ashraf and his companions asked Muhammad who would testify he was God's messenger; the answer is that God witnesses his delivery and their rejection.
rows.anchor: وروي أن كعب بن الأشرف وأصحابه قالوا: يا محمد! من يشهد بأنك رسول الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says those who believe in falsehood believe in anything besides God.
rows.anchor: والذين آمنوا بالباطل. قال ابن عباس: بغير الله

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqātil interprets falsehood as worship of Satan; another view identifies idols.
rows.anchor: وقال مقاتل: بعبادة الشيطان. وقيل: بالصنم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh demand punishment as a challenge and mockery, including al-Naḍr's request for stones; the appointed term is fixed by God and wisdom, with other views identifying Judgment Day, the interval between trumpet blasts, or Badr.
rows.anchor: ويستعجلونك: أي كفار قريش في قولهم

rows.speaker: ابن جبير وابن سلام
rows.claim: Ibn Jubayr identifies the appointed term as Judgment Day and Ibn Salām as the interval between trumpet blasts; another view says Badr, where punishment arrived suddenly.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير: يوم القيامة. وقال ابن سلام: أجل ما بين النفختين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Punishment will come unexpectedly; Hell already surrounds unbelievers, and يوم يغشاهم is accusative in connection with محيطة.
rows.anchor: وليأتينهم بغتة: أي فجأة، وهو ما ظهر يوم بدر

rows.speaker: الكوفيون ونافع
rows.claim: The Kufans and Nāfiʿ read ويقول with yāʾ, referring to God; others use the majestic nūn or one for the angels, while other readers report taʾ for Hell and passive يُقال.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكوفيون، ونافع: ويقول: أي الله وباقي السبعة: بالنون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After saying the earth is spacious and hinting at migration, God addresses fear that leaving home risks livelihood: each soul dies at its appointed time wherever it settles, and all return at Resurrection.
rows.anchor: ولما أخبر تعالى بسعة أرضه، وكان ذلك إشارة إلى الهجرة

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: ʿAlī reads ترجعون in the active voice; the majority read it passive in direct address, and a report from ʿĀṣim has the third person.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علي: ترجعون، مبنيا للفاعل والجمهور: مبينا للمفعول

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abū Ḥayyah reads ذائقة with nunation and الموت in the accusative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة: ذائقة، بالتنوين الموت: بالنصب

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read لنبوئنهم from المباءة, making an abode; cited constructions show بوأ taking two objects or a lām complement.
rows.anchor: وقرأ: لنبوئنهم، من المباءة. وقرأ علي، وعبد الله

rows.speaker: علي وعبد الله والربيع بن خثيم وابن وثاب وطلحة وزيد بن علي وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: These readers derive the form from الثواء, meaning to remain; this intransitive verb becomes transitive with causative hamza or doubling.
rows.anchor: وقرأ: لنبوئنهم، من المباءة. وقرأ علي، وعبد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The abode reading means God makes believers a dwelling and refuge; غرف are upper chambers, construed as a direct object or as a locative with a dropped preposition.
rows.anchor: والمعنى: ليجعلن لهم مكان مباءة، أي مرجعا يأوون إليه

rows.speaker: ابن عامر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir reads غرف with a rounded rāʾ.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عامر: غرفا، بضم الراء

rows.speaker: ابن وثاب
rows.claim: Ibn Waththāb reads فنعم with an added fāʾ; the majority omit it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب: فنعم، بالفاء والجمهور: بغير فاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The patient endure leaving their homelands, migration, and every hardship in obeying commands and avoiding prohibitions; patience and reliance on God comprise all good.
rows.anchor: الذين صبروا: أي على مفارقة أوطانهم والهجرة وجميع المشاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Muslims in Mecca were ordered to migrate, they feared poverty as strangers without homes, property, or anyone to feed them; the animals' example reassures them that God provides even for creatures unable to stock provisions.
rows.anchor: ولما أمر رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم، من أسلم بمكة بالهجرة، خافوا الفقر

rows.speaker: مجاهد وأبو مجلز وعلي بن الأقمر
rows.claim: They explain لا تحمل رزقها as not transporting or storing food; a report warns that hiding a year's supply betrays weak certainty.
rows.anchor: قاله مجاهد، وأبو مجلز، وعلي بن الأقمر. والادخار جاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another possible derivation means animals cannot provide for themselves or reliably feed themselves.
rows.anchor: قيل: ويجوز أن يكون من الحمالة التي لا تتكفل لنفسها

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Ḥasan says animals do not carry provisions because they do not store food; God feeds them each morning.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن: لا تحمل رزقها: لا تدخر، إنما تصبح فيرزقها الله

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says only humans, ants, mice, and magpies store provisions; a bulbul stores in its cheek pouches, while magpies forget their caches.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: لا يدخر إلا الآدمي والنمل والفأرة والعقعق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Animals may not store because weakness prevents them or because they lack reason to plan ahead; God provides for humans too, despite their earning and planning, and knows their fear of poverty.
rows.anchor: وانتفاء حملها لرزقها، إما لضعفها وعجزها عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: People admit God created the world, controls the sun and moon, and revives dead earth; that acknowledgment obliges them to recognize Him alone as provider, making their idol worship incoherent.
rows.anchor: ولما أخبر بأنهم مقرون بأن موجد العالم، ومسخر النيرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun in له can mean one person has provision expanded at one time and restricted at another, or that a different person is meant in each half, as in the cited lifespan and dirham constructions.
rows.anchor: والضمير في له ظاهره العود على من يشاء، فيكون ذلك الواحد

rows.speaker: علقمة الحمصي
rows.claim: ʿAlqama al-Ḥimṣī reads ويقدر with the passive pattern; عليم means God knows what benefits or harms His servants.
rows.anchor: وقرأ علقمة الحمصي: ويقدر: بضم الياء وفتح القاف وشد الدال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling worldly life هذه الدنيا belittles it: because it vanishes quickly and its people die, it is like children's play for an hour before they separate.
rows.anchor: وما هذه الحياة الدنيا: الإشارة بهذه ازدراء للدنيا وتصغير لأمرها

rows.speaker: الخليل وسيبويه
rows.claim: Al-Khalīl and Sībawayh take الحيوان as the verbal noun of حيِيَ; here it means the enduring abode of life. Mujāhid says there is no death there; another explanation calls the living person by the verbal noun.
rows.anchor: والحيوان، والحياة بمعنى واحد، وهو عند الخليل وسيبويه مصدر حيي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The afterlife is called حیّاً hyperbolically for its life; فعلان marks movement and agitation, and the لو clause leaves its answer implicit: people would not choose the perishable if they knew.
rows.anchor: وجعلت الدار الآخرة حيا على المبالغة بالوصف بالحياة

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: At sea polytheists call on God alone as if believers; al-Zamakhsharī connects this to their described idolatry, and Abū Ḥayyān calls the reference to the sincere a touch of mockery.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: بم اتصل قوله: فإذا ركبوا في الفلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: إذا هم يشركون reports an immediate return to their settled habit of associating partners after rescue.
rows.anchor: وإذا هم يشركون: جواب لما، أي فاجأ السجية إشراكهم بالله

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority treat the lām in ليكفروا as purpose and coordinate وليتمتعوا: they return to shirk to deny God's gifts and enjoy worldly goods, unlike rescued believers who grow more grateful and obedient.
rows.anchor: والظاهر في ليكفروا أنها لام كي، وعطف عليه وليتمتعوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second view takes the lām in both verbs as an imperative, supported by a silent lām in وليتمتعوا; this is a threat like the command to do as one wishes.
rows.anchor: وقيل: اللام في: ليكفروا، وليتمتعوا، لام الأمر

rows.speaker: الزمخشري
rows.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī says the apparent command to sin is figurative for abandonment and divine displeasure; Abū Ḥayyān notes that التحلية والخذلان are Muʿtazilite terms.
rows.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فإن قلت: كيف جاز أن يأمر الله تعالى بالكفر

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود وأبي
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿūd and Ubayy read فتمتعوا فسوف تعلمون in direct address; Abū al-ʿĀliya reads فيتمتعوا passively, and Ibn Masʿūd is also reported with لسوف تعلمون.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن مسعود: فتمتعوا فسوف تعلمون، بالتاء فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reminds Quraysh of their secure town despite its small population and barren setting: no one attacks or seizes them, a great gift only God can grant.
rows.anchor: ثم ذكرهم تعالى بنعمه، حيث أسكنهم بلدة أمنوا فيها

rows.speaker: الجمهور والسلمي والحسن
rows.claim: Most readers use third-person forms for يؤمنون and يكفرون; al-Sulamī and al-Ḥasan address listeners directly.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: يؤمنون، ويكفرون، بالياء فيهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fabrication is saying God has a partner, and denying the truth is rejecting the Messenger and Qur'an; لما جاءه shows they dismissed truth as soon as it arrived without reflection.
rows.anchor: وافتراؤهم الكذب: زعمهم أن لله شريكا، وتكذيبهم بالحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أليس rhetorically confirms Hell as their destination; explicit للكافرين replaces the implied pronoun مثواهم, with a poetic question offered as a parallel.
rows.anchor: وأليس تقرير لمقامهم في جهنم كقوله: ألستم خير من ركب المطايا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The unqualified striving includes struggle against the lower self, Satan, and religious enemies; cited explanations are examples rather than limits.
rows.anchor: أطلق المجاهدة، ولم يقيدها بمتعلق، ليتناول المجاهدة في النفس الأمارة بالسوء

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says striving means mastering desires to obey God, thank Him, and endure His trials.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس:

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says they strive by remaining firm in faith, so God guides them along paths to Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال السدي: جاهدوا فينا بالثبات على الإيمان

rows.speaker: أبو سليمان الداراني
rows.claim: Abū Sulaymān al-Dārānī says those who strive in what they know are guided to what they do not know.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو سليمان الداراني: جاهدوا فيما علموا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view explains striving as military jihad, leading to guidance toward martyrdom and forgiveness.
rows.anchor: وقيل: جاهدوا في الغزو، لنهدينهم سبل الشهادة والمغفرة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās identifies the muhsinūn at the verse's end as monotheists; another view says they are the strivers.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: المحسنين الموحدين. وقال غيره: المجاهدون

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن المبارك
rows.claim: Ibn al-Mubārak advises anyone stuck on a difficult question to ask people stationed at the frontier, relating this to God's guidance of strivers.
rows.anchor: وقال عبد الله بن المبارك: من اعتاصت عليه مسألة، فليسأل أهل الثغور عنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الذين is a subject with an omitted oath as its predicate and لنهدينهم as response; this rejects Thaʿlab's denial that an oath and its answer can predicate a subject.
rows.anchor: والذين: مبتدأ خبره القسم المحذوف، وجوابه: وهو لنهدينهم

none: Qur'an verses are quoted without commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra is Meccan; Ibn ʿAbbās exempts three verses beginning ولو أنما في الأرض, while Qatāda exempts two beginning there. Another view says it was revealed in Medina except those three verses.
rows.anchor: هذه السورة مكية، قال ابن عباس: إلا ثلاث آيات، أولهن: ولو أنما في الأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reported occasion is that Quraysh asked about Luqmān's story with his son and honoring parents, prompting the revelation.
rows.anchor: وسبب نزولها أن قريشا سألت عن قصة لقمان مع ابنه، وعن بر والديه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preceding claim that the Torah and its reports were little compared with God's knowledge led to revelation of the verse about trees as pens; this appears in the report about what the Jews said to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: التوراة وما فيها من الأنباء قليل في علم الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The sūra connects to the preceding one, which says the Qur'an gives every kind of parable: الم and the description of the Wise Book introduce it. Its closing challenge about a sign also anticipates the arrogant rejection in 31:7; تلك can signal exalted rank or distance.
rows.anchor: ومناسبتها لما قبلها أنه قال تعالى: ولقد ضربنا للناس في هذا القرآن من كل مثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: آيات الكتاب may mean the Qur'an or the Preserved Tablet.
rows.anchor: وآيات الكتاب: القرآن واللوح المحفوظ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الحكيم may mean containing wisdom, rarely may be an intensive pattern with passive sense 'made firm', or may mean judge. Al-Zamakhsharī offers 'possessing wisdom' and further grammatical explanations involving God's attribute or an omitted noun.
rows.anchor: ووصف الكتاب بالحكيم، إما لتضمنه للحكمة، قيل: أو فعيل بمعنى المحكم

rows.speaker: الجمهور والزمخشري
rows.claim: The majority read هدى ورحمة in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase governed by the demonstrative's pointing sense; al-Zamakhsharī and others give this parsing, which Abū Ḥayyān says needs scrutiny.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: هدى ورحمة، بالنصب على الحال من الآيات

rows.speaker: حمزة والأعمش والزعفراني وطلحة وقنبل
rows.claim: These readers raise هدى ورحمة, as a predicate after an omitted subject or a second predicate under grammarians who allow it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة، والأعمش، والزعفراني، وطلحة، وقنبل، من طريق أبي الفضل الواسطي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The المحسنين do the good deeds listed—prayer, almsgiving, and certainty about the afterlife—and are singled out because they benefit from the Qur'an and perceive it truly.
rows.anchor: للمحسنين: الذين يعملون الحسنات، وهي التي ذكرها. كإقامة الصلاة

rows.speaker: أوس
rows.claim: A verse by Aws illustrates الألمعي as perceptive, one who thinks about you as if he had seen and heard; al-Aṣmaʿī reportedly answered a question about the word by reciting it alone.
rows.anchor:
ونظيره قول أوس:
الألمعي الذي يظن بك ال ...

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Other explanations identify the المحسنين as people doing all good deeds, believers, the fortunate (Ibn Salām), or the successful (Ibn Shajara); the three named deeds are singled out for merit, and a hadith defines ihsan as worshipping as though seeing God.
rows.anchor: وقيل: المحسنون: المؤمنون. وقال ابن سلام: هم السعداء. وقال ابن شجرة
